author: John of Damascus
occasion: A concise doctrinal summary distinguishing the theology of the Trinity from the economy of the Incarnation, likely for instruction or clarification of orthodox faith.
argument: In the theology of the Trinity, one God is glorified and worshipped in three persons, with one divinity, nature, essence, power, authority, and will, while each person retains a distinct property: the Father is unbegotten, the Son is begotten, and the Spirit proceeds. The Father is without beginning, the Son is co-beginningless though from the Father, and the Holy Spirit is co-eternal and co-beginningless, proceeding from the Father not by filial generation but by procession. In the economy of the incarnate Word, two natures are confessed in one person, Jesus Christ, God together with man, with two wills and two energies, each nature keeping its property without division or confusion. The divine nature raises the dead and performs miracles, while the human nature is to hunger and thirst and grow weary, and to endure sufferings. The Word was united to flesh without confusion or division, ascended with that flesh, sits at the Father's right hand, and will come in glory at the end of the ages to judge the living and the dead as God incarnate.

outline.move: Introduces the topic and states the Trinitarian confession: one God in three persons with one divinity, nature, essence, power, authority, and will, each person having a distinct property.

Explains the eternal relations of the three persons: the Father without beginning, the Son co-beginningless from the Father, and the Spirit co-eternal proceeding from the Father, with the three being one in divinity.
Turns to the economy of the Incarnation, confessing two natures in one person of Christ, with two wills and two energies, each nature keeping its property without division or confusion.
Distinguishes the properties of each nature in Christ and affirms his ascension, session at the Father's right hand, and future return in glory to judge the living and the dead.

cast.name: Father
cast.who: The first person of the Trinity; his property is being unbegotten, and he is without beginning.

cast.name: Son
cast.who: The second person of the Trinity; his property is being begotten.

cast.name: Holy Spirit
cast.who: The third person of the Trinity; his property is proceeding.

cast.name: Jesus Christ
cast.who: The incarnate Son of God, our Lord, God together with man in one person.

key_terms.sense: The doctrine of the Trinity in itself, as distinct from the economy of salvation.
God's plan of salvation enacted in the Incarnation of the Word.
A distinct concrete reality or person, used for the three in the Trinity and the one in Christ.
The common being or essence shared by the three divine persons.
Nature, used for the one divine nature in the Trinity and the two natures in Christ.
Person or face, used interchangeably with hypostasis for the Trinity and for the one person of Christ.
The distinctive property or characteristic belonging to each divine person or each nature of Christ.
The Father's property of being unbegotten, without origin from another.
The Son's property of being begotten from the Father.
The Spirit's property of proceeding from the Father, distinct from generation.
Without division, describing how the two natures are united in Christ.
Without confusion, describing how the two natures remain distinct in Christ.
Will, one in the Trinity and two in Christ corresponding to his two natures.
Activity or operation, two in Christ corresponding to his two natures.
Flesh, referring to the human nature assumed by the Word in the Incarnation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: the Son is co-beginningless though from the Father
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Θεὸς ὁ Υἱὸς συνάναρχος, εἰ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρός
_unresolved_facts.fix: the Son is co-beginningless (συνάναρχος), though from the Father

_unresolved_facts.claim: the Holy Spirit is co-eternal and co-beginningless
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Θεὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, συναΐδιον καὶ συνάναρχον
_unresolved_facts.fix: the Holy Spirit is co-eternal (συναΐδιον) and co-beginningless (συνάναρχον)

_unresolved_facts.claim: proceeding from the Father not by filial generation but by procession
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὐχ υἱϊκῶς γεννώμενον ὡς Υἱὸς, ἀλλ' ἐκπορευτῶς
_unresolved_facts.fix: not begotten filially as the Son, but by procession (ἐκπορευτῶς)

_unresolved_facts.claim: The divine nature raises the dead and performs miracles, while the human nature is to hunger and thirst and grow weary, and to endure sufferings
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἴδιον μὲν γὰρ τῆς θεότητος, τὸ νεκροὺς ἀνιστᾷν, καὶ τὰς θεοσημείας ἐπιτελεῖν· ἴδιον δὲ τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος, τὸ πεινῇν καὶ διψῇν καὶ κοπιᾷν, καὶ τὰ πάθη ὑπομένειν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The property of the divinity is to raise the dead and perform divine signs; the property of the humanity is to hunger and thirst and grow weary, and to endure sufferings
